SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I, Special Branch
REPORT
No. D. 5674.
Date 8. 2. 1934.
Date February 6, 1934.

Subject (in full) Trouble between loafers and representatives of
mosquito newspapers.

Made by/ and Forwarded by D.S.I. Duncan

In connection with attached file relating to trouble
between a party of loafers and representatives of mosquito
newspapers which took place at about 9 p.m. January 31 in the
offices of the "Diamond" newspaper at No.5 Dz An Li, Tientsin
Road, a study of the matter does not reveal any connection
with the case in which the offices of the Great Crystal, a
mosquito newspaper published at 659 Ningpo Road, were entered
and damaged by five persons on September 2, 1933.

K.sec D3886/38.
In the case of the Great Crystal, enquiries showed
that the trouble undoubtedly originated from the fact that the
proprietor had printed articles alleging that certain of the
associations responsible for the collection of funds for the
support of the anti-Japanese armies in the North East had
appropriated part of these funds for their own use. As a
result of these publications it is alleged that the proprietor
of the Great Crystal was paid a certain sum of money to refrain
from continuing this unwanted publicity. When this became
known amongst the proprietors of other mosquito newspapers
they immediately endeavoured to obtain a share of the money
on the strength of the fact that they had also printed articles
relating to the alleged misappropriation of the funds. Being
unsuccessful, one Tsah Tiau Doo (蔡釣徒), editor of the
Loong Pao (龍報), accompanied by several loafers called at
the offices of the Great Crystal and on finding the editor out
smashed a few articles of the furniture and then left. Tsah
Tiau Doo was subsequently arrested, charged with malicious
damage and fined $30.

The present case which took place in the office of
the "Diamond" mosquito newspaper, No.5 Dz Ah Li, Tientsin

事由（全称） 无业游民与小报代表之间的纠纷。

编制人/转发人：特别调查科督察邓肯 (D.S.I. Duncan)

关于附件中涉及的一伙无业游民与小报代表之间于1月31日晚9时许在天津路慈安里5号“金钢钻”报社办公室发生的纠纷，经研究此事，并未发现其与1933年9月2日五人闯入并破坏位于宁波路659号的小报《大晶报》(Great Crystal) 办公室一案有任何关联。

K.sec D3886/38.
在《大晶报》一案中，调查显示，纠纷无疑源于该报业主刊登文章，指控某些负责为支援东北抗日军队募集资金的协会挪用了部分资金供己使用。据称，由于这些刊物的出版，《大晶报》业主收受了一定数额的金钱，以停止这种不受欢迎的宣传。当其他小报业主得知此事后，他们立即试图凭借自己也刊登了有关涉嫌挪用资金文章这一事实，从中分得一杯羹。因未成功，龙报 (Loong Pao) 编辑蔡釣徒 (Tsah Tiau Doo) 带领几名无业游民前往《大晶报》办公室，发现编辑不在后，砸坏了几件家具便离开了。蔡釣徒随后被捕，被控恶意破坏财物，并被罚款30元。

本案发生在天津路慈安里5号“金钢钻”小报办公室，是

At 9.15 p.m. 31-1-34, a telephone message was received from the occupants of No.5 Dz An Li (慈安里) off Tientsin Road, reporting that a number of loafers was there causing trouble and requesting Police assistance.
On receipt of this information a party of Police attended, but on arrival, found that the loafers had absconded.
As result of enquiries made by the undersigned and D.I. Sih (薛) of the Special Branch, who had attended this Station in response to a telephone call sent to him by D.S.I. Duncan, who had been informed of the occurrence by the undersigned, it was ascertained from one named Sz Tsih Chun (施志春) representing the "Diamond" (金钢钻) Mosquito newspaper that at 9.p.m. 31-1-34, the following newspaper respresentatives had met at his offices at No.5 Dz An Li off Tientsin Road for purpose of holding a meeting, the purpose of which was to discuss the possibility of forming a joint sales office for all mosquito newspapers. general opinion of the various newspaper representatives
who attended this meeting, is that to-night's attack is
one of revenge against the two aforesaid newspapers, for
having printed certain facts regarding the Red Pill case.
Inquiries in the alleyway etc. revealed that
altogether about 20 loafers visited this address, but
only eight went upstairs and after the incident all
dispersed on Tientsin Road taking different directions.
